recent_works.title: Photothermal Antibacterial and Antioxidant Fe-Polyphenol Poly(lipoic acid) Patches for Infected Burn Wounds
recent_works.abstract: Infected burn wounds remain challenging to treat because bacterial contamination and oxidative stress can jointly compromise tissue repair. Herein, we report an adhesive supramolecular elastomer patch (PLCTF) constructed from a dynamic poly(α-lipoic acid) network reinforced by Fe-polyphenol coordination and hydrogen bonding. The reversible disulfide chemistry of lipoic acid contributes to network adaptability, resulting in improved mechanical performance and conformal adhesion on moist skin-like biological tissue surfaces. Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, PLCTF converted the incident NIR light into localized heat, thereby further enhancing PLCTF-mediated antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli under controlled irradiation conditions. In addition, the polyphenolic motifs and lipoic acid-related components provided radical-scavenging activity, as evidenced by chemical radical-scavenging assays and intracellular ROS fluorescence analysis. PLCTF also showed favorable hemocompatibility and cytocompatibility, including after short-term NIR exposure, and promoted fibroblast migration. Hydrostatic load-bearing capacity of porosity-affected filament-wound egg-shaped pressure hulls: RVE-based material characterization and numerical assessment
recent_works.abstract: This study addresses a critical challenge in composite pressure vessels where pore defects, inevitably introduced during manufacturing, significantly compromise structural integrity and safety performance. An investigation is therefore conducted into the failure mechanisms of filament-wound egg-shaped pressure hulls containing such defects. Representative Volume Elements featuring circular, elliptical, and cylindrical pores were developed. Based on homogenization theory, the macroscopic equivalent material properties were predicted utilizing the maximum stress criterion and the maximum principal stress criterion. These derived micro-scale parameters were subsequently incorporated into a macro-scale progressive failure analysis framework for the filament-wound egg-shaped hull. By integrating the 3D Hashin failure criterion with a fracture energy-based damage evolution model, the effects of dominant pore morphology, shape factor, winding layer and liner thickness, and slip coefficient on the ultimate bearing capacity were systematically evaluated. recent_works.title: A multi‐source fusion and dynamic verification framework for scientific knowledge graph construction: Methods, evaluation, and applications
recent_works.abstract: Abstract The exponential growth of scientific literature—over 2.5 million papers and 3.5 million patents annually—poses critical challenges for knowledge discovery. To address these, we propose SCIMKG (Scientific Knowledge Graph), a framework for constructing scientific knowledge graphs via multi‐source heterogeneous multi‐source. To address these challenges, we propose SCIMKG (Scientific Knowledge Graph), a framework for constructing scientific knowledge graphs through multi‐source heterogeneous multi‐source. SCIMKG integrates diverse academic resources including research papers, patents, experimental datasets, videos, charts, and tables to automate the construction of domain‐specific knowledge graphs. Our framework introduces three key innovations: (1) a multi‐source entity fusion mechanism employing Graph Attention Networks (GATs) with composite similarity metrics for cross‐source alignment; (2) a dynamic hybrid verification pipeline integrating semantic, statistical, and rule‐based methods; and (3) a Domain‐Adaptive Relation Extraction model (DA‐RE) utilizing adversarial training and prototype networks. recent_works.title: Synergistic Surface Engineering of Sustainable Polyurethane: Flame Retardancy, Kinetics, and Multiphase Oil Adsorption Perspectives
recent_works.abstract: Abstract Severe threats posed by oil spill incidents to aquatic ecosystems have increased the demand for green, circular, and sustainable materials to mitigate these problems. Biobased polyurethane sponge (BS) derived from renewable resources serves as an excellent candidate; however, the inherent flammability and poor hydrophobicity hinder its practical use in oil spill remediation. Herein, we introduce a multifunctional surface modification approach for these matters. A coating containing reduced graphene oxide (RGO), diammonium hydrogen phosphate (DAP), and stearic acid (SA) was applied to BS to fabricate the modified sponge (BS-RDS). This modification imparted the BS with self-extinguishing behavior and markedly enhanced its flame retardancy; notably, a UL-94 V-0 rating was achieved when the BS was coated with a 10 wt % DAP solution. In parallel, the surface hydrophobicity of the modified BS was significantly improved, with an increase in the water contact angle to 134°. Moreover, the BS-RDS demonstrated effective oil adsorption capacities ranging from 11 to 40 g/g, depending on oil type, and retained 7–9 times its own weight after 10 cycles.
